newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA STATE BUDGET DEFICIT RISES IN NOVEMBER.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA STATE BUDGET DEFICIT RISES IN NOVEMBER.

text.p: Romania's state budget deficit widened to 4.19 trillion lei ($768.8 million) at end-November from 3.66 trillion in the first 10 months of 1996, official data showed on Wednesday.
Eleven-month spending was 20.19 trillion lei, up from 17.87 trillion at end-October. State revenues rose to 15.99 trillion lei over January-November from 14.21 trillion in the first 10 months.

Overspending by the former leftist government in the 1996 election campaign led to a soaring public deficit estimated to account for 5.7 percent of gross domestic product at the end of 1996, against a target of 2.2 percent.
The International Monetary Fund suspended loan tranches for Romania last year over foreign exchange market restrictions, slow reforms and lax budgetary discipline.

Romania's new centrist coalition government, formed after general elections last November, is now negotiating a new loan accord with the IMF. Talks on loans are also under way with the World Bank and the European Union.
The new cabinet, which pledged to strengthen financial discipline and cut taxes, has yet to draft a 1997 state budget.
The IMF reccomended Romania to quickly tackle the budget deficit issue and consider further spending carefully.
-- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1-3120264 ($ = 5450 Romanian Lei)
